prerequisites: Basic concepts of analysis, including differentiation of functions with multiple variables.
Basic concepts of general physics and chemistry (scientific track ASO level).

learning_outcomes.text: The student can explain and interrelate the fundamental concepts and principles of thermodynamics.
The student can build thermodynamic reasoning and elaborate simple applications based on these concepts.
The student is aware of the role and scope of thermodynamics within various engineering disciplines.

syllabus_topics: Introductory concepts: Systems, equilibrium states and state variables; the zeroth law of thermodynamics; equilibrium and non-equilibrium state changes; isochoric, isobaric, isothermal and adiabatic processes.

Properties and processes of pure fluids: Equation of state for ideal and real fluids; the ideal gas law; polytropic state changes; co-existence of vapor and liquid; thermotechnical tables and diagrams.

The first law of thermodynamics: Work and heat; process characteristics versus state variables; specific heat; the first law of thermodynamics for closed and open systems; internal energy and enthalpy, including the main property of enthalpy; technical work; Joule's experiment and its consequences for ideal gases.

Applications of the first law of thermodynamics to Joule-Kelvin expansion, throttling processes, nozzles and diffusers, work and heat exchangers, cyclic processes, and to equilibrium and non-equilibrium state changes in general.

The second (and third) law of thermodynamics: Reversible and irreversible state changes; different formulations of the second law; the Clausius principle; refrigerators and heat pumps; the Kelvin-Planck principle and thermal engines; Carnot's theorems, Carnot's cycle and Carnot's cycle with irreversible heat exchanges; Clausius' inequality; the thermodynamic temperature scale and absolute temperatures.
The concept of entropy and the calculation of entropy changes for open and closed systems; statistical probability as a measure of entropy; the third law of thermodynamics and its interpretation.

Thermodynamic equilibrium: Available energy; the characteristic functions internal energy, enthalpy, Gibbs free energy and Helmholtz free energy; fundamental equations, identities, Maxwell relations and partial derivatives, with application examples; two-phase equilibrium in one-component systems; the Clausius-Clapeyron equation; univariant two-phase equilibrium and vapor pressure.
Non-chemically reacting complex systems with generalized work exchanges: Uniaxial deformation of an elastic material; uniaxial deformation of a dielectric elastic material in an electric field.

Systems with variable composition and (electro)chemical reactions: The chemical potential and partial molar quantities; relationships between extensive state variables and the derived integral and partial molar quantities; thermodynamic equilibrium in heterogeneous systems; chemical potentials of components in pure gases and pure condensed substances, ideal-gas mixtures and condensed solutions; Raoultian activity; ideal Raoultian solutions; mixing quantities and excess quantities.
Calculation of reaction and formation enthalpies (thermochemistry); reaction equilibria; electrochemical equilibrium and the Nernst equation.
Applications of the first law of thermodynamics (2 sessions)
Applications of the second law of thermodynamics (2 sessions)
Two-phase equilibrium, gas mixtures and solutions (1 session)
Generalized thermodynamic equilibrium and combination of phase and chemical equilibrium (1 session)
